verses.1: For Jehovah will have mercy on Jacob, and again choose Israel. He will place them on their land. The foreigners will be cursed over them, and they will be incorporated into the family of Jacob.
verses.2: And they were taken away by nations, and brought to their place. They were placed in the houses of Israel, on the land of Jehovah, to serve as servants and wives. They remained there, and their children also lived there.
verses.3: And it shall be on that day that Jehovah will take away from you all your troubles and sorrows, as well as the hard work that you have been subjected to.
verses.4: And you took this king as a prey for Babylon. And you said, “How can you return to Medeba?”
verses.5: The LORD has broken the power of the wicked who rule over others.
verses.6: May those nations be destroyed through violence. May they be scattered far away from us. May they be pursued without any hope of survival.
verses.7: May peace reign over all the land; may there be no more destruction.
verses.8: Even the trees were happy for you. Arzey Levonan, since you were laid down, the tree no longer rises above us.
verses.9: Shaul is under a curse; he will cause you trouble. He’s a source of harm for you. All the kings of the nations have built their altars on his behalf.
verses.10: They will all answer and say, “You too, you are like us. You have been punished just like us.”
verses.11: Your enemy will try to deceive you, but he will fail. He will try to deceive you, but he will not succeed.
verses.12: How did you fall from heaven? You, son of darkness, have come down to the earth, to afflict the nations.
verses.13: And you said in your heart, “The heavens shall rise from above, like the stars of heaven. I will sit on a throne in heaven, and I will reign over all things.”
verses.14: I will climb up onto the steep hill of Edom.
verses.16: Do you see that they will watch over you? They will nurture and care for you. This man is a scourge to the land; he disgards the kings.
verses.17: Tiber was turned into a desert, and its cities were destroyed. Its prisoners were not allowed to enter the temple at all.
verses.18: All the kings of the nations slept in comfort, each in his own house.
verses.19: And you have thrown away your remains as an object of disgust and shame. They are like corpses that have been left on the rocks, like offerings to the gods.
verses.20: Do not join them in death, for your land has been destroyed; you have killed your people. Let no evil seed be sown forever.
verses.21: They prepared for their children a place of refuge in the wilderness, so that they could not be destroyed. They would inherit the land, and cities would fill the shores of the sea.
verses.22: And I stood upon them, O LORD, with Your army. I recognized Babylon as its name. And all the other cities as well. O LORD!
verses.23: And she was placed upon the slopes of hills and rivers, and her waters flowed like tears. May the Lord, the Almighty, have mercy on her.
verses.24: May the Lord, in His army, bless us, saying: “If not for what I have decreed, it would not have happened. And as I have commanded, so it shall be.”
verses.25: To destroy Assyria in my land, and to remove them from their hills. They will be driven away from their positions, and they will be overthrown from their thrones.
verses.26: This is the counsel that has been given for all the earth. And this is the hand that controls all the nations.
verses.27: For Jehovah’s army has given orders; who can break them? And whose hand is strong enough to move them, and who can restore them to their place?
verses.28: In the year of King Ahaz’s death, this was the time when the curse came upon him.
verses.29: Let not you be glad, O Philistia! For a kingdom has been destroyed from its roots. As a snake’s venom is burned away, so too will its power be destroyed.
verses.30: And they suffered greatly among the poor and needy. They surely would die from hunger. Your roots will be destroyed, and your remaining parts will also perish.
verses.31: Hail, gate of lamentation! O city of sorrow! All is lost, for smoke has risen from the sky, and there is no one to comfort those who are in pain.
verses.32: And what will those wicked people answer when Jehovah establishes a sanctuary in it, so that the poor of his people may dwell there?
